answer: One identity costs one climb: the applicant hikes to a canyon plot the registry assigns, plants a willow there, and signs the summit marker as a ranger watches. Contours go out in order — first the canyon floor, then the first ridge — so the k-th identity climbs to the k-th contour, a longer trail and scarcer permit each time. One body cannot climb twice at once, and each contour is assigned only after the last identity is minted, so no batching. Forging 1,000 puppets takes 1,000 climbs at $40 plus $30 per contour, about $15,055,000; one honest trip to the canyon floor costs $70.
